prompt: Recommend movies to a user based on what similar users rated highly.
tells: based on what similar users rated highly
why: Use the user–item ratings matrix to find similar tastes.
trap: Clustering users is coarser than learning each user's preferences.

prompt: Show "customers who bought this also bought" on product pages.
tells: customers who bought this also bought
why: Item-to-item collaborative filtering from co-purchase data.
trap: No product attributes are needed, only behavior.

prompt: You have 2 million users and 500,000 songs, but each user has played under 0.01% of the songs.
why: Matrix factorization learns low-dimensional user and item vectors from sparse interactions.
trap: Standard PCA struggles with mostly-missing data; factorization is built for it.

prompt: A recommender works well for long-time users but shows random items to new users who have no history.
tells: new users who have no history
why: The cold-start weakness of collaborative filtering: fall back to popularity or content features until history builds.
trap: Bandits can help explore, but the issue to name is CF's need for history.

prompt: Suggest songs a listener hasn't heard, based on listening patterns of people with similar taste.
tells: listening patterns of people with similar taste
why: Learn from user–song interactions which songs similar users enjoy.
trap: Clustering puts listeners in buckets; recommendations need per-user scores.

prompt: A shopping app has no ratings, only views, add-to-carts and purchases. Build product recommendations from these.
tells: no ratings, only views, add-to-carts and purchases
why: Implicit-feedback matrix factorization (for example ALS) weights stronger signals more.
trap: No explicit ratings doesn't rule out CF; it changes the loss.

prompt: On each book page, show "readers of this book also read", computed from millions of reading histories.
tells: readers of this book also read
why: Item–item similarity from co-occurrence in user histories.
trap: Book metadata isn't needed; the behavior is the signal.

prompt: A recommender keeps suggesting the same 50 blockbuster titles to everyone, and niche items never get shown.
why: Popularity bias in CF: normalize for popularity, re-rank for diversity, and add exploration.
trap: A bandit can add exploration, but the issue to name is the recommender's bias.
